authentication: none; optional free API key for a higher daily quota
cost_notes: free; no SLA and no commercial support; FDA may throttle or restrict access per its terms
entity_identifiers: k_number and pma_number (clearance references carried on the establishment record)
UNKNOWN - no UDI-DI at establishment level
free_tier: free; 1,000 req/day per IP without a key
historical_coverage: current registrations plus recently expired ones; it is a living register, not an archive
known_limitations: establishment-level, not product-level: one record describes who may distribute what, so it must never be counted as a second clearance record
the registration object's sub-fields were only inspected at key level in this probe, so its date semantics are explicitly UNKNOWN here
a registration is not evidence of marketing: registered establishments routinely hold listings for products that were never launched
company linkage must use registration.name, which is again a filed legal string
licence: public domain: FDA dedicates openFDA content/data to the public domain under a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication (open.fda.gov/license/, verified)
rate_limits: documented: 240 requests/min and 1,000 requests/day per IP without a key; 240/min and 120,000/day with a free key (open.fda.gov/apis/authentication/, verified). `skip` is capped at 25,000, so full history requires splitting by decision_date windows
research_value: Gives the manufacturing/distribution footprint behind a clearance: which establishments list which product codes, including contract manufacturers. That is the only openFDA endpoint that connects a company's regulatory identity to its physical production and import network, which matters for supply-chain questions the clearance stream cannot answer.
timestamp_fields: UNKNOWN - the probe verified the top-level record keys only; the establishment object's own date fields were not enumerated, so no event clock is claimed for this source
update_frequency: continuous; 337,116 records in the 2026-11-02 export (2 partitions)
